_note: Volumes come from the cluster's default storage class; the claim template names none, so the lab is portable. On a WaitForFirstConsumer class a claim stays Pending until its Pod is scheduled, which is why the PVC checks poll. verify-pvc-kept-after-scaledown asserts the claim SURVIVES scale-down (the Kubernetes default) — a cluster configured with a persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy that deletes it makes the check fail loudly, which is correct since the page's claim would not hold there. imagePullPolicy is not patched here: a StatefulSet's Pod template edit would trigger an ordered rollout mid-lab.

steps.run: envsubst < statefulset.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc rollout status statefulset/hello-dcs --timeout=300s
for i in 0 1; do oc exec hello-dcs-$i -- sh -c 'echo "written by $HOSTNAME" > /opt/app-root/src/data/owner.txt'; done; echo wrote markers
for i in 0 1; do printf 'hello-dcs-%s: ' "$i"; oc exec hello-dcs-$i -- cat /opt/app-root/src/data/owner.txt; done
oc delete pod hello-dcs-0 && oc rollout status statefulset/hello-dcs --timeout=180s
oc scale statefulset/hello-dcs --replicas=3 && oc rollout status statefulset/hello-dcs --timeout=300s
oc scale statefulset/hello-dcs --replicas=2 && oc rollout status statefulset/hello-dcs --timeout=180s
oc get pods -l app=hello-dcs && oc get pvc
